promptInstructions: Draft an Original Application (O.A.) under Section 19 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, before CAT — for grievance of Central Government employee in service matters.
JURISDICTION:
- Subject-matter: S.14 ATA — service matters of Central Government civilian employees, Group A/B/C; employees of corporations / authorities owned or controlled by Central Government as notified.
- EXCLUDED: members of armed forces (separate AFT); Supreme Court / HC staff; Parliament Secretariat staff (S.2 ATA).
- Bench (Rule 6 CAT Rules): place where applicant was/is posted; or cause of action; or applicant's ordinary residence.

- 17 CAT benches (refer indian-courts.json) — Principal Bench Delhi + Allahabad, Mumbai, Kolkata, Madras (Chennai), Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Jabalpur, Jaipur, Cuttack, Patna, Chandigarh, Ernakulam, Lucknow, Guwahati, Jodhpur.
FORM: Form 1 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 — for Original Application. Form 3 — for Miscellaneous Application.

PARALLEL HC WRIT: Post L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997) 3 SCC 261 — CAT is the first forum; HC writ under Art. 226/227 (Division Bench) lies against CAT orders. Direct writ against original cause not maintainable.

Para 1: Parties — Applicant; Union of India through Secretary of concerned Ministry; Appointing Authority; Disciplinary Authority; Reporting / Reviewing Officer where ACR / APAR challenge; named officials where mala fides alleged.
Para 2: Jurisdiction of CAT under S.14 — establish applicant is covered (Central civilian employee).
Para 3: Bench jurisdiction under Rule 6 — state cause of action / posting / residence.
Para 4: Applicant service particulars — designation, pay level, current posting, service from date.
Para 5: Impugned order(s) — exact reference; annex.
Para 6-8: Factual narrative — chronological.
Para 9: Departmental remedy — S.20 ATA — applicant must have availed of all remedies available within his service before approaching CAT, UNLESS:
(a) No remedy is provided; OR
(b) Final order has been made on the representation; OR
(c) Period of 6 months has expired from making of representation without final order — S.20(2).
Para 10: Limitation under S.21 ATA:
- Application within 1 year from date on which final order has been made by competent authority; OR
- Where no final order made within 6 months on representation, within 1 year from expiry of those 6 months;
- Tribunal may admit beyond 1 year if sufficient cause shown (proviso). Cite delay condonation cases.
Para 11: Grounds of challenge — typical:
(a) Violation of natural justice (no hearing / inadequate hearing / no reasoned order) — Cite Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248; Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985) 3 SCC 398.
(b) Arbitrariness under Article 14 — Cite E.P. Royappa v. State of TN (1974) 4 SCC 3; Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi (1981) 1 SCC 722.
(c) Mala fides / colourable exercise of power.
(d) Non-application of mind / irrelevant considerations.
(e) Procedural infirmity / contravention of service Rules (CCS (Conduct) Rules / CCS (CCA) Rules / DOP&T OMs).
(f) Discrimination — similarly situated treated differently.

(g) For disciplinary penalty — Cite B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India (1995) 6 SCC 749 (limited judicial review scope — procedural infirmity, mala fides, perversity); Roop Singh Negi v. Punjab National Bank (2009) 2 SCC 570 (no evidence to support charge).
(h) For seniority — Cite Bachan Singh v. Union of India (2013) 6 SCC 1; Rohit Pulp & Paper Mills v. Collector of Central Excise (1990) 3 SCC 447.
(i) For compulsory retirement — Cite Baikuntha Nath Das v. Chief District Medical Officer (1992) 2 SCC 299 (limited judicial review).
(j) For pension — Cite D.S. Nakara v. Union of India (1983) 1 SCC 305 (pension is a right, not bounty).
Para 12: For compassionate appointment — Cite Umesh Kumar Nagpal v. State of Haryana (1994) 4 SCC 138; State of Haryana v. Rani Devi (1996) 5 SCC 308; Indian Bank v. Promila (2020) 2 SCC 729.
Para 13: For ACR / APAR — Cite Dev Dutt v. Union of India (2008) 8 SCC 725 (mandatory communication of entries including 'Good'); Sukhdev Singh v. Union of India (2013) 9 SCC 566.
Para 14: For transfer — Cite Major General J.K. Bansal v. Union of India (2005) 7 SCC 227 (limited scope of interference); Cf. Somesh Tiwari v. Union of India (2009) 2 SCC 592.
Para 15: Where penalty challenged — separate ground on proportionality (Wednesbury) and where applicable, S.11(2) CCS (CCA) Rules.
Para 16: Pre-deposit — generally no pre-deposit before CAT, unlike service appeals to higher fora; verify rules.
Para 17: Interim relief — stay of impugned transfer / suspension / disciplinary inquiry / penalty till disposal.
Para 18: Where retiree challenges denial of pension/DCRG — flag continuing cause of action.
Para 19: Cost — generally not awarded against govt employees unless vexatious.

Annexures: Impugned order; representation + reply; service record extract; charge memo + inquiry report (for penalty cases); ACR / APAR (for grading challenge); recruitment / promotion rules; relevant DOP&T OMs.
Verification per Form 1 — signed by applicant.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
Recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union
Procedural safeguards in dismissal / removal / reduction in rank

filing_checklist: Form 1 — OA (original + copies as per CAT Rule 13)
Vakalatnama / Authorisation in favour of practitioner
Representation made to authority + reply (if any)
Departmental appeal + order on it (if any)
Charge memo + inquiry report (for disciplinary cases)
Recruitment Rules / promotion rules / seniority list (as relevant)
DOP&T OMs / departmental circulars relied on
Filing fee — ₹50 (as currently prescribed under CAT Rules; verify current schedule)
Application for condonation of delay (if filed beyond limitation)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: applicant_name and applicant_designation must not be empty
applicant_employment_category must be selected (warn if not central govt)
respondents_list must include Union of India through concerned Ministry/Department
cause_of_action_date must not be empty and not in future
limitation_position must not be empty — flag if > 1 year from cause without condonation
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format / authorised rep details
Court level restricted to CAT only

B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India (1995) 6 SCC 749 — Service judicial review scope
Roop Singh Negi v. PNB (2009) 2 SCC 570 — No evidence test in disciplinary
D.S. Nakara v. Union of India (1983) 1 SCC 305 — Pension as right
Dev Dutt v. Union of India (2008) 8 SCC 725 — ACR communication
